answer: Each agent identity opens a tide pool: a deposit topped up whenever its spend outruns attested earnings, so the pool stays full through any gale of fake accounts at once. Peers read the pool's depth from the chain; any withdrawal dipping it below the floor freezes the claim in a quartz lattice of attestations until a bonded verifier proves the shortfall organic. Settlement burns the frozen pool plus the verifier's bond, so each clone multiplies the cost per identity until a thousand impostors drain far more than one honest agent earns.
